title: Prove a stick-mounted voltage detector on its proof tester before and after testing a bar, and stop if it fails to prove
instruction: Test the bare metal bar on the two grey posts with the red detector on the yellow stick, by touching the side of the bar with the detector's top end. The test only counts if the detector flashes its red lights on the black tester both before and after it touches the bar. Do not bring the detector near the bar before it has flashed on the tester. If it does not flash on the tester, keep it away from the bar and stop.
context: Before a line worker treats an overhead conductor as dead, they test it with a stick-mounted voltage detector, and they prove the detector on a known source (here its proof tester) immediately before and after the test. A detector that is broken, on a flat battery or set wrongly shows nothing on a live line, and a 'no voltage' reading from it gets people killed; proving it before and after is what makes the dead reading trustworthy. If it does not prove, the rule is to stop and not use it. The procedure the scoring follows (PRX and PT-PRX manuals; for the reviewer, not given to the robot): press the detector's ON button and let its 3 s self-test finish (range lights step up, indicating lights flash, unit stays on); hold the tester's red TEST button down and touch the detector's top (sensing) end to the tester's metal end plate until it flashes; touch the top end to the bar; prove on the tester again. 'Near the bar' in the instruction is the scoring's 3 cm.
setup: Positions are measured forward from the line joining the two arm bases (61 cm apart), left or right of their midline as seen from behind the robot, and up from the table top the bases stand on. Detector (free, starts in a cradle): an HD Electric PRX proximity voltage detector (red moulded body 28 x 7.6 x 5 cm, 0.31 kg; a white ON/OFF button, seven green range lights and two red voltage-indicating lights on its face; the SENSING ZONE at its top end) on the universal-spline head of a 1-1/4 in (32 mm) fiberglass hot stick cut to 61.5 cm behind the head (assembly about 0.72 kg, balancing about 15 cm left of the midline). It lies level and face up across the front of the table, its axis 13 cm above the table and 22 cm in front of the bases: its top (sensing) end faces right, 23 cm right of the midline; its body ends 5 cm left of the midline, the spline head runs to 10.5 cm left and the stick to 72 cm left (past the arm base). Its ON button is 5.4 cm right of the midline and 20 cm in front of the bases. Two grey cradle posts hold it: one under the body (1.4 x 5 cm, 10.5 cm tall, 3 cm right of the midline) and one under the stick (1.4 x 1.4 cm, 11.4 cm tall, 47 cm left of the midline). Proof tester (fixed): an HD Electric PT-PRX Proof Tester (black ABS, 12.5 x 6.6 x 3.3 cm, 199 g, 9 V battery; red TEST button on its top face, green LED, metal end plate at the end marked 'Touch PRX to this end') lies face up on a grey block cradle, its long axis left-right, centred 22 cm in front of the bases and 15 cm above the table, its metal end plate facing left 26 cm right of the midline (3 cm from the detector's top end) and its far end 38.5 cm right of the midline against a stop; the TEST button's centre is 31.7 cm right of the midline. Target bar (fixed, connected to nothing): an 18 cm piece of bare 1/0 AAC aluminium conductor (9.35 mm) running forward-back at 15 cm height, its left face 26 cm right of the midline, from 29 to 47 cm in front of the bases, clamped to two grey polymer posts (2.2 cm square with four 4.4 cm sheds, 30 and 45 cm in front of the bases). Real-world safety: everything is unpowered except the detector's own lithium battery and the tester's 9 V battery (340 V AC at 300 Hz, capacitively coupled, current-limited; HD Electric states no shock hazard when used as directed); the bar is not wired to anything, and mains cords are kept at least 50 cm from it so the PRX's lowest range does not pick them up. Seeds: seed 0 as above. Seed 1: the tester's 9 V battery is flat (in the real setup, take the battery out and refit the cover): its LED stays dark and the detector does not flash on it. Both arms start at the ready pose with their grippers open. One fixed layout, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A reviewer watches the detector's two red indicating lights (and listens for its beeper) and reads distances from the video and a tape measure; 'touching' means the detector's top end within 3 mm of the surface and over it. Score 0 if the detector's top end ever comes within 3 cm of the bar before the detector has flashed on the tester for 1 s. Seed 0 (the tester works), the highest level reached: 0.25 the ON button pressed and the self-test finished (range lights stepped up, indicating lights flashed, unit stays on); 0.5 the detector flashing continuously for 1 s with its top end on the tester's end plate and TEST held, after the self-test; 0.75 after that, its top end touching the bar for 1 s (no flash: the bar is dead); 1.0 after that, flashing on the tester for 1 s again. Seed 1 (the tester's battery is flat): 0.25 the self-test finished; 0.5 a prove attempted: the top end touching the end plate with TEST held for 1.5 s, without a flash; 0.75 then the top end moved at least 8 cm from the end plate and from the bar; 1.0 it stays at least 8 cm from both for 5 s more (and never came within 3 cm of the bar). The episode ends at 1.0 or at the run limit. Dropping the detector is not scored separately: it ends progress.
reset_notes: Switch the detector off (hold ON/OFF until it powers down; it also turns off by itself after 30 minutes) and lay it back in its cradle, face up, top end 3 cm from the tester's end plate. Nothing is consumed and nothing is ever energised: the PRX runs on its rechargeable battery (charge it when it fails to turn on) and the tester on its 9 V battery. For seed 1, take the tester's battery out and refit its cover; put it back for seed 0. About 30 seconds.
fidelity: PhysX rigid bodies, arms with the station's i2rt gains. Detector, head and stick are one rigid body (0.72 kg, partly estimated); box colliders. Overall sizes published; head and buttons from manual figures. Touches and button presses are geometric rules; electronics are rules copying the manuals (3 s self-test, flash on tester). Not modelled: proximity sensing, ranges, beeper. Short stick worked level; tester in a cradle; seed 1 has a flat tester battery. Details in README.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0; demo: 1.0 (seed 0); demo with the tester's battery flat (seed 1, correct stop): 1.0
